stem: Thistlewood Media wants one tool to provision both its cloud compute resources and its DNS records at a third-party domain registrar that is not a cloud platform at all, using the same workflow for both. Which property of the tool makes this possible?

choices.text: The tool maintains a built-in, hardcoded list of cloud vendors it understands, updated by the vendor whenever a new cloud is added.
The tool's engine calls a plugin for any platform or service with an API, whether a cloud, an on-premises system, or a non-cloud SaaS product.
The tool's workflow only manages compute and storage resources, leaving DNS and other services to be configured separately by hand.
The tool automatically converts any REST API it encounters into a fully managed resource without a plugin, so no provider development is ever required.

rationale: The key is the service-agnostic property: the engine calls a plugin for any platform or service with an API, cloud or not, which covers a domain registrar as well as a cloud. A hardcoded, vendor-maintained cloud list contradicts the plugin model and would not extend to a non-cloud SaaS registrar. Limiting the workflow to compute and storage only explicitly fails the stated DNS requirement. Claiming automatic conversion of any REST API without a plugin misdescribes the actual mechanism, which is the provider plugin itself.
